relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with an LAD-I diagnosis ("A 9 years old girl affected by LAD-1"); no ITGB2 variant or genetic testing is reported, so she is in scope by diagnosis only.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). The father is mentioned only as giving consent, so he gets no row. No ITGB2 variant, genetic test or CD18 assay result is printed for the patient, so the variants table is empty. '9 years old' is the age when the knee abscess developed; the course then lasted more than a year, so it is used as onset of the abscess feature only, not as age at last evaluation or diagnosis. Laboratory values (WBC 23,000 mm3 with 86% neutrophils, hemoglobin 8 g/dL, CRP 106 mg/dL) are recorded as stated; the paper does not call them leukocytosis, so the checklist item 'leukocytosis or neutrophilia' is left not reported. Positive blood cultures and 'bacteremia episodes' are recorded as features, but the paper never says sepsis for her, so 'sepsis' is not reported. Apparent contradiction over time: 'no bone lesion was found' at the EG admission versus later 'X-ray radiography showed bone lesions'; both rows emitted, no checklist item affected. 'Healing was complete but poorly formed' was mapped to 'impaired wound healing' observed. Country/ethnicity, consanguinity and vital status are not stated.

treatment_summary.value: amikacine and imipenem for three weeks plus local disinfection (knee abscess); constant prophylaxis with sulfamethoxazole + trimetoprime and itraconazole; targeted antibiotic and anti-fungal therapy with amphotericine B via a Broviack central catheter; then granulocyte pocket transfusions with G-CSF, liposomal amphotericine B, amphotericine B, flucytosine and targeted antibiotics, after which the EG lesion disappeared
span: She was treated with amikacine 400 mg/day and imipenem 400 × 2 mg/day for three weeks and local disinfection
she was constantly under prophylactic treatment [25 mg/Kg/2 days (sulfamethoxazole + trimetoprime) and 10 mg/Kg/day Itraconazole]
a Broviack central catheter for amphotericine B administration was installed

we started transfusions of irradiated, phenotyped granulocytes pockets (3 pockets per week in median) along with G-CSF 5 μg/Kg/day; liposomal amphotericine B (Abelcet 2 mg/Kg/day), amphotericine B (0,3 mg/Kg/day up to 2 mg/Kg/day), flucytosine, and targeted antibiotics
After almost 5 months of such treatment cultures became negative, EG reduced progressively and then disappeared completely
